title: Official OTS ConvIR-B signed high-demand overshoot measurement on SOTS-Outdoor
rationale: The completed paired-GT correction measurement rejected the claim that high-demand regions are corrected less strongly, but its unsigned MSE ratio cannot distinguish accurate recovery from crossing beyond GT. This orthogonal measurement-target route uses the same fixed OTS checkpoint and complete SOTS population, defines high-demand tiles only from paired input error, and measures signed projection beyond GT with both relative and absolute materiality guards. It performs no training, threshold selection or protected-data access.

orthogonal_changes.reason: The prior unsigned relative-correction estimand cannot determine whether strong high-demand correction crosses beyond paired GT; signed projection and material residual magnitude answer a substantively different question.

scientific_contract.question: Across 492 independent SOTS-Outdoor clear-source groups, does the fixed official OTS ConvIR-B baseline show materially prevalent signed overshoot beyond paired GT in the highest-demand 20 percent of input-error tiles?

intervention.reference: paired hazy input to clear GT direction, with high-demand tiles defined before inference from the top 20 percent of paired input MSE
intervention.matched_budget: all 500 hazy variants nested within exactly 492 clear-source groups; one fixed official checkpoint; zero training or model selection
fixed_factors: all 492 GT images and all 500 paired hazy images are used at original resolution with no scientific-data resizing
official Dehazing.OTS build_net('base') is strictly loaded from checkpoint state_dict['model']; input is reflect-padded to a multiple of 32 and model(input)[2] is cropped and clipped to [0,1]
non-overlapping 32 by 32 tiles are formed after reflect-padding all image arrays only to a multiple of 32
high-demand tiles are the exact top 20 percent of tile mean RGB input-to-GT squared error with stable row-major tie breaking
for each tile, signed projection coefficient alpha is dot(prediction-input, GT-input) divided by squared norm(GT-input) plus 1e-8
signed projected overshoot magnitude is max(alpha minus 1, zero) times the RMS norm of GT-input in the tile
a tile is materially overshot only when alpha is at least 1.05 and projected overshoot magnitude is at least 1/255
a hazy variant is high-demand overshot when at least 20 percent of its high-demand tiles are materially overshot
a source group is high-demand overshot when the arithmetic mean high-demand overshot-tile fraction across its variants is at least 20 percent
multiple hazy variants are averaged within their clear-source group before the group indicator; variants, tiles and pixels are never independent samples
missing or failed source groups remain visible and prevent a definitive PASS or FAIL

primary_estimand.metric: proportion of 492 independent clear-source groups whose variant-mean materially overshot fraction among high-demand tiles is at least 0.20
primary_estimand.aggregation: source-group binary indicator with two-sided Wilson 95 percent interval

controls: strict identity-bound official OTS checkpoint and official production graph
full-image input-to-output MSE improvement as a global-competence prerequisite
paired GT defines both restoration direction and high-demand regions independently of model output
alpha equals zero for unchanged input, one for exact GT, and 1.10 for a synthetic ten-percent extension beyond GT
absolute 1/255 projected-overshoot guard excludes numerically trivial crossings
all hazy variants nested and averaged within the original clear-source group

uncertainty.method: two-sided Wilson 95 percent intervals over 492 independent clear-source groups; variants, tiles and pixels remain nested

gates.estimand: checkpoint, model sources, prior completed local-error closeout, complete SOTS pairing and aggregate dataset identity match
independent source groups with every paired variant and finite inference
Wilson lower 95 percent bound for source groups whose variant-mean full-image output MSE is below input MSE
Wilson interval for source-group high-demand signed-overshoot prevalence

scientific_contract.competing_explanation: Projection beyond paired GT along the input-to-GT vector operationalizes directional overshoot but does not prove perceptual over-dehazing: RGB GT may contain alignment, color or compression differences, clipping can hide larger excursions, and SOTS clear-source overlap with OTS training is not excluded. Passing would establish a descriptive paired-GT overshoot pattern for this fixed model, not a causal haze mechanism or automatic need for a new module.
disabled_actions: training, fine-tuning, module insertion, loss selection, threshold tuning or candidate selection during this route
using model output to define high-demand regions or source groups
interpreting unsigned MSE improvement alone as overshoot
treating paired RGB projection as a pure perceptual dehazing-strength label or causal mechanism evidence
treating SOTS outcomes as strict unseen-source generalization because clear-source overlap with OTS training is not excluded
relabeling SOTS as confirmation or sealed-final evidence after this development-screening use
Haze4K outcome, NH-HAZE, confirmation, canary or locked-test access
changing image membership, preprocessing, grouping, metrics, margins, controls or terminal rules after outcomes

precision_contract.rationale: All 492 source groups exceed the 475 groups required for a worst-case two-sided 95 percent binomial-proportion half-width of 0.045.

capability.production_path_statement: The exact official Dehazing.OTS build_net('base') graph strictly loads the official OTS checkpoint and executes the production reflect-pad-to-32, model(input)[2], crop, clip, paired-GT signed projection and result-finalizer path on one synthetic CUDA tensor without scientific data.

precision.source_reference: The asset audit established 492 independent clear-source groups; ceil(1.96^2*0.25/0.045^2)=475.
